name: Mobile Security
description: Security and privacy of Android and iOS apps, permissions, app stores, and mobile platforms.
narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security work in this list centered on the cat-and-mouse of analyzing Android apps. A cluster of 2018 papers attacked the core problem that apps actively resist inspection: "Tackling runtime-based obfuscation in Android with TIRO" (2018) targeted malware that hides behavior at runtime, "FlowCog: Context-aware Semantics Extraction and Analysis of Information Flow Leaks in Android Apps" (2018) reasoned about whether information flows were legitimate, and "Discovering Flaws in Security-Focused Static Analysis Tools for Android using Systematic Mutation" (2018) turned the lens on the analysis tools themselves, showing they miss real leaks. In parallel, "ATtention Spanned: Comprehensive Vulnerability Analysis of AT Commands Within the Android Ecosystem" (2018) showed that the attack surface reached down into legacy modem interfaces, hinting that mobile security was about far more than app bytecode.

Around 2019-2020 the field broadened from the app layer toward the whole mobile platform and its trust boundaries. Researchers dug into Apple's wireless stack with "A Billion Open Interfaces for Eve and Mallory" (2019), into pre-installed firmware apps with "FIRMSCOPE: Automatic Uncovering of Privilege-Escalation Vulnerabilities in Pre-Installed Apps in Android Firmware" (2020), and into hardware-backed trust with "PARTEMU: Enabling Dynamic Analysis of Real-World TrustZone Software Using Emulation" (2020). At the same time, privacy moved to center stage: "Actions Speak Louder than Words: Entity-Sensitive Privacy Policy and Data Flow Analysis with PoliCheck" (2020) automatically checked whether apps' actual data flows matched what their privacy policies promised, reframing compliance as a measurable security property.

By 2021 two trends matured. First, ecosystem-scale measurement of long-standing problems, exemplified by "Why Eve and Mallory Still Love Android: Revisiting TLS (In)Security in Android Applications" (2021) and the human-centered "A Large Scale Study of User Behavior, Expectations and Engagement with Android Permissions" (2021), and the supply-chain-flavored "Understanding Malicious Cross-library Data Harvesting on Android" (2021). Second, machine learning became both a defense and a target, opening with "Explanation-Guided Backdoor Poisoning Attacks Against Malware Classifiers" (2021).

The most recent work shows the area splitting along two frontiers. On the ML side, robustness and drift now dominate: "Continuous Learning for Android Malware Detection" (2023) confronts concept drift, while "Black-box Adversarial Example Attack towards FCG Based Android Malware Detection under Incomplete Feature Information" (2023) attacks detectors directly. On the physical and emerging-platform side, side channels and new form factors take over, from "Eavesdropping Mobile App Activity via Radio-Frequency Energy Harvesting" (2023) to AR/VR threats like "Going through the motions: AR/VR keylogging from user head motions" (2023), signaling that mobile security is expanding from phones toward the next generation of wearable and immersive devices.

milestones.title: Tackling runtime-based obfuscation in Android with TIRO
milestones.note: anchored the early agenda of defeating runtime obfuscation so Android malware could actually be analyzed

milestones.title: Discovering Flaws in Security-Focused Static Analysis Tools for Android using Systematic Mutation
milestones.note: turned scrutiny onto the analysis tools themselves, exposing how often they miss real leaks

milestones.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Entity-Sensitive Privacy Policy and Data Flow Analysis with PoliCheck
milestones.note: reframed privacy as automatically checking app data flows against the policies apps promise

milestones.title: FIRMSCOPE: Automatic Uncovering of Privilege-Escalation Vulnerabilities in Pre-Installed Apps in Android Firmware
milestones.note: pushed the field past third-party apps to the privileged pre-installed apps baked into firmware

milestones.title: Explanation-Guided Backdoor Poisoning Attacks Against Malware Classifiers
milestones.note: marked the pivot to treating ML malware classifiers themselves as an attack surface

milestones.title: A Large Scale Study of User Behavior, Expectations and Engagement with Android Permissions
milestones.note: brought a global, human-centered lens to whether the permission model actually works for users

milestones.title: Continuous Learning for Android Malware Detection
milestones.note: confronted concept drift, the core obstacle to keeping ML malware detectors useful over time

milestones.title: Going through the motions: AR/VR keylogging from user head motions
milestones.note: extended mobile security to emerging AR/VR platforms via a novel sensor-based side channel
